items.text: Capability map exists: module table with stable kebab-case ids, one line each, dependency direction; if two modules each need the other, they are one module
All interfaces are marked PROVISIONAL (freeze happens after feasibility); a post-feasibility recheck also binds the final interface and freeze artifacts
Every failure mode is phrased as an on-call question ('how do I know X is stuck?')
Risk classes defined for this project: which task classes are 'high' (get blind tester + independent reviewer + doubt loop)
Trust boundaries named; abuse cases written next to use cases for each boundary
Module contract cards created in docs/modules/ (purpose, interface, invariants, state transitions, commands, recovery)

redFlags: An interface frozen before the feasibility model ran
A module whose card cannot state its invariants
Failure modes listed as nouns ('bridge failure') instead of on-call questions

rationalizations.excuse: The architecture is obvious for this size
rationalizations.reality: The map costs ten lines. Getting module boundaries wrong costs every later phase.
